title: Port Authority Act
full_text:
Chapter 1 General Provisions <Amended 2010.2.4>

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to contribute to the development of the national economy by establishing port authorities to enhance the expertise and efficiency of work concerning the development, management, and operation of port facilities, thereby developing ports into competitive hubs for shipping and logistics.

Article 2 (Relationship to Other Acts)
Except as provided in this Act, Article 16, Article 22(1), Article 25(5), Article 31(6), Article 34(1), subparagraph 2, Article 35, Article 36(2), Articles 38 and 39, and Article 48(8) of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions shall apply mutatis mutandis to the organization, operation, etc. of port authorities. <Amended 2012.6.1>

Article 3 (Guarantee of Autonomous Operation)
The State shall guarantee the autonomous operation of port authorities to establish a system of accountable management for port authorities.

Article 4 (Legal Personality, Etc.)
(1) A port authority (hereinafter referred to as an "Authority") shall be a legal entity.
(2) Authorities shall be established for individual ports, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, in consideration of the conditions at the relevant port (meaning a trade port under Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Harbor Act; the same shall apply hereinafter). However, where necessary for the efficiency of the development, management, and operation of port facilities, etc., an Authority with jurisdiction over two or more adjacent ports may be established. <Amended 2016.12.20>
(3) Matters necessary for the procedures for establishing an Authority, etc. shall be prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries. <Added 2016.12.20>
(4) The area of jurisdiction of an Authority shall be the port area (meaning a port area under Article 2, subparagraph 4 of the Harbor Act; the same shall apply hereinafter) of a port prescribed by Presidential Decree. However, where necessary for the smooth performance of its business, an Authority may also exercise jurisdiction over port facilities and other facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree outside port areas. <Amended 2016.12.20>

Article 5 (Offices)
(1) The location of an Authority's principal office shall be prescribed by its articles of incorporation.
(2) Where necessary for the performance of its business, an Authority may establish a branch or sub-office following a resolution of the port committee under Article 10.

Article 6 (Capital Contributions)
(1) Notwithstanding the State Property Act and the Public Property and Commodity Management Act, the State or a local government may contribute to an Authority movable and immovable property necessary for the Authority's business and rights to manage port facilities under Article 24 of the Harbor Act (hereinafter referred to as "rights to manage port facilities"). In such cases, the value of the capital contribution of rights to manage port facilities shall be based on market value pursuant to statutes and regulations governing State property. <Amended 2019.1.8, 2020.1.29>
(2) Capital contributions to an Authority under paragraph (1) shall be governed by the State Property Act and Article 28 of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act.
(3) An Authority may request that the State (meaning the administrative agency managing the certificates of equity interests in the port authority; the same shall apply hereinafter in this Article) or the head of a local government convert assets received as contributions in kind from the State or a local government into rights to manage port facilities and contribute those rights.
(4) Where the State or the head of a local government receiving a request for conversion of a capital contribution under paragraph (3) deems the conversion necessary, it shall, after consulting with the heads of relevant administrative agencies, determine whether to approve the request or the scope of approval.
(5) Assets subject to a request for conversion of a capital contribution under paragraph (3) shall be deemed transferred to the State or local government upon approval under paragraph (4), and the right to manage the port facilities corresponding to those assets shall be deemed contributed. In such cases, the return value of the assets being returned shall be the book value of the contributed assets at the time of return, and the contribution value of the rights to manage port facilities into which the contribution is converted shall be based on market value pursuant to statutes and regulations governing State property. <Amended 2019.1.8>
(6) An Authority shall obtain approval from the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries or the head of a local government when dividing or consolidating rights to manage port facilities received as capital contributions, or transferring or contributing them to a third party or using them as the subject of a mortgage. <Amended 2013.3.23>

Article 7 (Registration)
(1) An Authority shall come into existence upon registration of its establishment with the court having jurisdiction over the location of its principal office.
(2) The provisions on registration in the Civil Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the registration of establishment under paragraph (1), the registration of the establishment or relocation of offices, registration of changes, and other registrations of an Authority.
(3) An Authority may not assert against a third party any matter requiring registration until it has registered that matter.

Article 8 (Business)
(1) An Authority shall perform the following activities: <Amended 2012.6.1, 2019.1.8, 2020.1.29, 2022.11.15>
1. Execution of construction works for the new construction, reconstruction, maintenance, repair, dredging, etc. of port facilities under Article 2, subparagraph 5 of the Harbor Act (excluding port facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as outer harbor facilities and port access transportation facilities), and activities concerning port management and operation, such as port guarding, security, cargo management, and passenger terminals.
2. Port hinterland complex development projects under Article 2, subparagraph 11 of the Harbor Act.
2-2. Port redevelopment projects under Article 2, subparagraph 4 of the Act on Port Redevelopment and Development of Surrounding Areas.
2-3. Activities concerning the development, management, and operation of marina facilities under Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Act on the Development and Management of Marinas.
3. The business of operating logistics facilities under Article 2, subparagraph 2(b) of the Framework Act on Logistics Policies.
4. Activities entrusted by the State or a local government in connection with the development, management, and operation of ports.
4-2. Activities concerning the installation, management, and operation of new and renewable energy facilities under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Act on the Promotion of the Development, Use and Diffusion of New and Renewable Energy, using sites and facilities managed by the Authority (limited to the extent that such activities do not contravene the purposes of port management and operation).
5. Activities concerning investigations, research, technological development, and personnel training relating to the activities under subparagraphs 1, 2, 2-2, 2-3, 3, and 4.
6. Activities concerning the construction and operation, outside port areas, of neighborhood living facilities, welfare facilities, etc. for the convenience of port users.
6-2. Exchange and cooperation activities between South and North Korea for the development, management, and operation of ports, etc.
6-3. Activities to carry forward and commemorate the achievements of hosting the Exposition under Article 4(2) of the Special Act on Commemoration and Post-Expo Utilization of the International Exposition Yeosu, and activities relating to post-Expo utilization.
7. Other activities prescribed by Presidential Decree as necessary to achieve the purposes for which the Authority was established, such as the development, management, and operation of ports in foreign countries.
8. Direct execution of, or capital contributions or contributions to, ancillary activities related to the activities under subparagraphs 1, 2, 2-2, 2-3, 3, 4-2, 6, 6-2, 6-3, and 7.
(2) Matters necessary concerning the costs incurred by an Authority in performing activities entrusted under paragraph (1), subparagraph 4, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) An Authority shall obtain approval from the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries to directly execute, or make capital contributions or contributions to, ancillary activities under paragraph (1), subparagraph 8. <Amended 2013.3.23>

Article 9 (Prohibition on Use of Similar Names)
A person other than an Authority under this Act shall not use the name "port authority" or any similar name.

Chapter 2 Port Committee

Article 10 (Establishment of the Port Committee)
A port committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee") shall be established within an Authority to deliberate and resolve upon the following matters:
1. Management objectives, budgets, funding plans, business plans, and operating plans.
2. Use of contingency reserves and carryover of budgets.
3. Settlement of accounts.
4. Acquisition and disposition of basic property.
5. Borrowing of long-term loans, issuance of corporate bonds, and repayment plans therefor.
6. Establishment of standards for rent and usage fees for port facilities.
7. Disposition of surpluses.
8. Investments and contributions.
9. Amendments to the articles of incorporation.
10. Establishment and amendment of internal regulations.
11. Appointment of members of the officer recommendation committee under Article 16-2.
12. Establishment of branches or sub-offices.
13. Other matters deemed particularly necessary by the Committee.

Article 11 (Composition)
(1) The Committee shall be composed of no more than 15 members appointed by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, who shall serve on a part-time basis. <Amended 2013.3.23>
(2) The members shall include persons recommended, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, by the metropolitan mayor, provincial governor, or special self-governing province governor having jurisdiction over the location of the relevant port (hereinafter referred to as a "Mayor or Governor"), and persons representing organizations of users of the relevant port. <Amended 2016.12.20>
(3) When recommending a member pursuant to paragraph (2), a Mayor or Governor shall present the criteria and reasons for the recommendation.
(4) The chairperson of the Committee shall be elected by and from among its members.
(5) Matters necessary concerning the composition of the Committee and the qualifications of its members, etc., other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (4), shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 11-2 (Requests for Removal from Office, Etc.)
(1) Where the Committee determines that there is a substantial impediment to the performance of the president's duties as head of the institution, such as where the president of the Authority commits an act in violation of statutes, regulations, or the articles of incorporation or neglects those duties, it may, following a resolution, request the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries to remove the president of the Authority from office. <Amended 2013.3.23>
(2) Members may, where deemed necessary, request the auditor to audit a specific matter relating to the operations of the Authority by a written request jointly signed by at least two members. In such cases, the auditor shall comply with the request unless there are special circumstances.
(3) A member may request the president of the Authority to provide data necessary for the performance of the member's duties. In such cases, the president of the Authority shall comply with the request unless there are special circumstances.

Article 12 (Terms of Office)
(1) The term of office of a member (including the chairperson; the same shall apply hereinafter in this Chapter) shall be two years, and a member may be reappointed for consecutive one-year terms. In such cases, the appointing authority shall decide whether to reappoint the member in consideration of the results of evaluations of the performance of duties and other performance of duties.
(2) Where a vacancy occurs among the members, a replacement member shall be appointed pursuant to Article 11.
(3) A member whose term of office has expired shall continue to perform the member's duties until a successor is appointed.

Article 13 (Disqualifications)
(1) A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall not be eligible to serve as a member of the Committee:
1. A person falling under any subparagraph of Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act.
2. A member of a political party.
3. A person registered as a candidate in an election held under the Public Official Election Act.
(2) Where a member comes to fall under any subparagraph of paragraph (1), the member shall automatically cease to hold office.

Article 14 (Meetings)
(1) The Committee shall be convened at the request of the chairperson or at least one-third of the incumbent members, and the chairperson shall preside over its meetings.
(2) The Committee shall adopt resolutions with the affirmative votes of a majority of its incumbent members.
(3) The president and auditor may attend meetings of the Committee and speak.
(4) Where necessary, the Committee may have relevant experts and others attend a meeting to hear their opinions.
(5) Matters necessary for the payment of allowances to members, etc. shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 15 (Exclusion of Members)
A member shall be excluded from deliberations and resolutions concerning any of the following matters. In such cases, members who may not participate in a resolution shall not be counted among the incumbent members under Article 14(2).
1. A matter in which the member has a direct interest.
2. A matter in which the member's spouse, a blood relative within the fourth degree, or a relative by marriage within the second degree has a direct interest.

Chapter 3 Officers <Amended 2010.2.4>

Article 16 (Appointment of Officers)
(1) An Authority shall have no more than five officers, including the president and auditor.
(2) The president shall be appointed by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, after consultation with the relevant Mayor or Governor, from among multiple persons recommended by the officer recommendation committee under Article 16-2. <Amended 2012.6.1, 2013.3.23>
(3) The auditor shall be appointed by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, in consultation with the Minister of Finance and Economy, from among multiple persons recommended by the officer recommendation committee under Article 16-2. <Amended 2012.6.1, 2013.3.23, 2025.10.1>
(4) Officers other than the president and auditor shall be appointed by the president. <Amended 2012.6.1>
(5) Article 13 shall apply mutatis mutandis to officers.
(6) Matters necessary for the appointment of officers, other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (5), shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. <Amended 2012.6.1, 2013.3.23>

Article 16-2 (Officer Recommendation Committee)
(1) An officer recommendation committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Recommendation Committee") shall be established within an Authority to recommend candidates for officers.
(2) The Recommendation Committee shall be composed of persons appointed by the Committee and some members of the Committee.
(3) Officers and employees of the Authority and public officials shall not be eligible to serve as members of the Recommendation Committee. However, this shall not apply to members of the Committee or teachers under the Educational Officials Act.
(4) The prescribed number of persons appointed by the Committee pursuant to paragraph (2) shall be less than one-half of the total prescribed membership of the Recommendation Committee.
(5) The members of the Recommendation Committee shall elect its chairperson from among those members who are members of the Committee.
(6) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Recommendation Committee, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 17 (Duties of Officers)
(1) The president shall represent the Authority, oversee its operations, and be responsible for its management performance.
(2) The president shall report to the Committee on the Authority's management performance and business plans and shall be obliged to comply with matters decided by the Committee.
(3) Where the president is unable to perform the president's duties for an unavoidable reason, one of the officers (excluding the auditor) shall act on behalf of the president as prescribed by the articles of incorporation. Where there is no such officer or no such officer can act on behalf of the president, a person prescribed by the articles of incorporation shall act on behalf of the president.
(4) The auditor shall audit the Authority's operations and accounts and submit opinions thereon to the Committee.

Article 18 (Terms of Office of Officers)
(1) The term of office of the president shall be three years, and the terms of office of officers other than the president shall be two years, and officers may be reappointed for consecutive one-year terms. In such cases, the appointing authority shall decide whether to reappoint an officer in consideration of the results of evaluations of the performance of duties and other performance of duties.
(2) An officer whose term of office has expired shall continue to perform the officer's duties until a successor is appointed.

Article 19 (Restriction on the President's Authority to Represent the Authority)
The president shall not represent the Authority in matters in which the interests of the Authority and the president conflict, and the auditor shall represent the Authority in such matters.

Article 20 (Appointment of Agents)
The president may, as prescribed by the articles of incorporation, appoint from among employees an agent with authority to perform all judicial or extrajudicial acts concerning the Authority's operations.

Chapter 4 Implementation of Projects and Finance

Article 21 (Execution of Port Facility Construction Works)
Notwithstanding Article 9(1) and the main clause of Article 9(2) of the Harbor Act, the Authority may execute construction works for the new construction, reconstruction, maintenance, repair, dredging, and other works on port facilities under subparagraphs 1, 2-3, and 4 of Article 8(1) (hereinafter referred to as "port facility construction works"). In such cases, the Authority shall comply with the port master plan under Article 5 of the Harbor Act and the master plan for marinas under Article 4 of the Act on the Development and Management of Marinas. <Amended on January 8, 2019>

Article 21-2 (Implementation of New Port Construction Projects)
(1) Notwithstanding Article 7 of the Act on Promotion of New Port Construction, the Authority may implement new port construction projects under subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of that Act (hereinafter referred to as "new port construction projects"). In such cases, the Authority shall comply with the master plan for new port construction under Article 3 of the Act on Promotion of New Port Construction. <Amended on June 1, 2012>
(2) The Authority shall not participate in a new port construction project pursued as a privately financed project by a project implementer under the Act on Public-Private Partnerships in Infrastructure. However, this shall not apply after a negotiating party under Article 13(2) of the Act on Public-Private Partnerships in Infrastructure has been designated. <Newly inserted on June 1, 2012>

Article 22 (Approval of Implementation Plans)
(1) Where the Authority intends to carry out port facility construction works or a new port construction project, it shall formulate a project implementation plan (hereinafter referred to as an "implementation plan") as prescribed by Presidential Decree and obtain approval from the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries. The same shall apply where the Authority intends to change approved matters. However, this shall not apply to facility construction works prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the paving of open storage yards or the installation of warehouses. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
(2) Deleted. <May 16, 2023>
(3) Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries approves an implementation plan (including amendments to an implementation plan; hereinafter the same shall apply), the Minister shall give public notice thereof in the Official Gazette. <Amended on March 23, 2013>

Article 23 (Deemed Authorizations and Permits, Etc. under Other Acts)
(1) Where the Authority obtains approval of an implementation plan for port facility construction works under Article 22, it shall be deemed to have obtained or completed the relevant authorizations, permits, licenses, approvals, decisions, designations, consultations, reports, releases, and other approvals or procedures listed below (hereinafter referred to as "authorizations, permits, etc.") for matters on which the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries has consulted in advance with the heads of the administrative agencies responsible for such authorizations, permits, etc.: <Amended on April 15, 2010; May 31, 2010; January 14, 2014; January 20, 2015; December 20, 2016; March 13, 2018; March 31, 2020; December 27, 2022; May 16, 2023>
1. Determination of urban and county management plans under Article 30 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act, permission to alter the form and quality of land and subdivide land under Article 56 of that Act, designation of implementers of urban and county planning facility projects under Article 86 of that Act, and authorization of implementation plans for urban and county planning facility projects under Article 88 of that Act;
2. Authorization of waterworks business under Articles 17 and 49 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act, and authorization for installation of private waterworks under Articles 52 and 54 of that Act;
3. Permission for construction works and other works concerning public sewerage under Article 16 of the Sewerage Act, occupancy permission under Article 24 of that Act, and reporting on the installation of private sewage treatment facilities under Article 34 of that Act;
4. Permission to occupy and use public waters under Article 8 of the Public Waters Management and Reclamation Act, approval or reporting of implementation plans for the occupation and use of public waters under Article 17 of that Act, a license to reclaim public waters under Article 28 of that Act, consultation and approval for reclamation of public waters undertaken by the State and other entities under Article 35 of that Act, and approval of implementation plans for reclamation of public waters under Article 38 of that Act;
5. A building permit under Article 11 of the Building Act, a building report under Article 14 of that Act, permission for or reporting of changes to matters covered by a building permit or building report under Article 16 of that Act, a permit for or report on the construction of temporary buildings under Article 20 of that Act, and consultation on construction under Article 29 of that Act;
6. Permission to execute river works under Article 30 of the River Act, and permission to occupy a river under Article 33 of that Act;
7. Consultation with or approval by the road management authority under Article 107 of the Road Act (limited to matters concerning the designation and public notice of road routes under Article 19 of that Act, determination of road areas under Article 25 of that Act, permission for road construction works and other works by persons other than the road management authority under Article 36 of that Act, and permission to occupy roads under Article 61 of that Act);
8. Permission for and consultation on conversion of farmland under Article 34 of the Farmland Act;
9. Permission for and reporting of felling standing timber and other activities under Article 36(1) and (5) of the Creation and Management of Forest Resources Act, and permission for and reporting of activities in forest protection zones (excluding forest genetic resource protection zones) under Article 9(1) and subparagraphs 1 and 2 of Article 9(2) of the Forest Protection Act;
10. Permission for and reporting of conversion of mountainous districts under Articles 14 and 15 of the Mountainous Districts Management Act, and permission for and reporting of temporary use of mountainous districts under Article 15-2 of that Act;
11. Permission to fell standing trees or bamboo, collect earth and rocks, tree roots or grass roots, or conduct other activities in erosion control areas under Article 14 of the Erosion Control Work Act, and cancellation of designation of erosion control areas under Article 20 of that Act;
12. Permission to establish manufacturing facilities and other facilities under Article 6(1) of the Act on the Safety Control of Hazardous Substances;
13. Permission to occupy and use parks under Article 23(1) of the Natural Parks Act, and consultation with the park management authority under Article 71 of that Act;
14. Approval of an implementation plan under Article 9(1) of the Special Act on Designation and Management of Free Economic Zones;
15. Approval of a business plan for a tourist accommodation business under Article 15 of the Tourism Promotion Act;
16. Approval for use of agricultural production infrastructure for purposes other than its intended purposes under Article 23 of the Agricultural and Fishing Villages Improvement Act, and approval of a development project plan for an agricultural and fishing village tourism and recreation complex under Article 82 of that Act;
17. Designation of an implementer of a marina development project under Article 9 of the Act on the Development and Management of Marinas, and approval of an implementation plan for a marina development project under Article 13 of that Act;
18. Approval of factory establishment and other matters under Article 13 of the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act, a building permit for or building report on a factory under Article 14 of that Act, approval for use of a factory building under Article 14-2 of that Act, approval for installation of manufacturing facilities under Article 14-3 of that Act, and approval for establishment of a knowledge industry center and other matters under Article 28-2 of that Act;
19. Permission for improvement of small rivers and other relevant areas by persons other than the management authority under Article 10 of the Small River Maintenance Act;
20. Approval for construction works in protected waters under Article 47 of the Fishery Resources Management Act;
21. Authorization or reporting of construction plans for electric installations for private use under Article 8 of the Electrical Safety Management Act;
22. Approval of, and approval of amendments to, implementation plans for railroad construction projects under Article 9 of the Act on Railroad Construction and Maintenance of Railroad Facilities;
23. Approval of a business plan for a sports facilities business under Article 12 of the Installation and Utilization of Sports Facilities Act;
24. Approval of an implementation plan for a housing site development project under Article 9 of the Housing Site Development Promotion Act.
(2) Where the Authority obtains approval of an implementation plan for a new port construction project under Article 22, it shall be deemed to have obtained the authorizations, permits, etc. under the subparagraphs of Article 9(2) of the Act on Promotion of New Port Construction for matters on which the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries has consulted in advance with the heads of relevant administrative agencies. <Amended on May 16, 2023>
(3) Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries gives public notice of approval of an implementation plan under Article 22(3), public notice or public announcement of the authorizations, permits, etc. under the relevant Acts listed in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) or the subparagraphs of Article 9(2) of the Act on Promotion of New Port Construction shall be deemed to have been given. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
(4) To approve an implementation plan or an amendment thereto under the main clause of Article 22(1), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall consult in advance with the heads of the competent administrative agencies on whether the plan complies with the relevant statutes and regulations under the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) and the subparagraphs of Article 9(1) of the Act on Promotion of New Port Construction. In such cases, the head of a competent administrative agency shall submit an opinion within the period prescribed by Presidential Decree from the date of receipt of the request for consultation. <Newly inserted on May 16, 2023>
(5) Except as provided for in paragraphs (1) through (4), Articles 24 through 26 of the Framework Act on Public Administration shall apply mutatis mutandis to the criteria and effects of deemed authorizations, permits, etc. and other relevant matters. <Newly inserted on May 16, 2023>

Article 24 (Confirmation of Completion)
(1) Upon completing port facility construction works or construction works for a new port construction project for which an implementation plan has been approved under Article 22, the Authority shall submit a construction completion report to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries without delay and obtain confirmation of completion. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
(2) Upon receiving an application for confirmation of completion under paragraph (1), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall conduct a completion inspection without delay and, where the Minister finds that the relevant port facility construction works have been completed in accordance with the implementation plan, issue a certificate of completion to the Authority and give public notice thereof in the Official Gazette. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
(3) Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries issues a certificate of completion under paragraph (2), a completion inspection, authorization of completion, or other procedure required under the authorizations, permits, etc. deemed obtained under the subparagraphs of Article 23(1) or the subparagraphs of Article 9(2) of the Act on Promotion of New Port Construction shall be deemed to have been completed or obtained. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
(4) No person shall use land or facilities developed or installed through port facility construction works or a new port construction project before a certificate of completion under paragraph (2) has been issued. However, such land or facilities may be used where a report has been filed with the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
(5) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall notify the person who filed a report under the proviso to paragraph (4) whether the report is accepted within three days from the date of receipt of the report. <Newly inserted on January 8, 2019>
(6) Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries fails to notify the person who filed the report, within the period prescribed in paragraph (5), whether the report is accepted or whether the processing period is extended under statutes and regulations governing the processing of civil petitions, the report shall be deemed accepted on the day following the last day of that period (meaning the extended processing period where the processing period is extended or further extended under statutes and regulations governing the processing of civil petitions). <Newly inserted on January 8, 2019>

Article 25 (Vesting of Port Facilities, Etc.)
(1) Upon completion of land development and installation of port facilities by the Authority with its own financial resources through port facility construction works or a new port construction project implemented after approval of an implementation plan under Article 22(1), the land and port facilities shall vest in the Authority.
(2) The Authority may donate to the State the land and port facilities vested in it under paragraph (1), pursuant to Article 13 of the State Property Act.
(3) The State may establish a right to manage port facilities in favor of the Authority that donated the land and port facilities under paragraph (2), in respect of that land and those port facilities. <Amended on January 8, 2019>

Article 25-2 (Relationship with Other Acts)
Except as provided for in Articles 21, 21-2, and 22 through 25, port facility construction works and new port construction projects shall be governed by the Harbor Act and the Act on Promotion of New Port Construction.

Article 26 (Expropriation of Land, Etc.)
(1) Where necessary for the performance of its projects, the Authority may expropriate or use land, objects, or rights under Article 3 of the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, Etc. for Public Works Projects (hereinafter referred to as "land, etc.").
(2) Where an implementation plan is approved and publicly notified under Article 22(1) and (3), project approval and public notice of project approval under Article 20(1) and Article 22 of the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, Etc. for Public Works Projects shall be deemed to have been given. In such cases, notwithstanding Article 23(1) and Article 28(1) of that Act, an application for adjudication on the expropriation or use of land, etc. shall be made within the project implementation period specified in the implementation plan.
(3) Except as provided for in this Act, expropriation or use under paragraph (1) shall be governed by the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, Etc. for Public Works Projects.

Article 27 (Gratuitous Lease of State or Local Government Property, Etc.)
(1) Where the State or a local government deems it necessary for the efficient implementation of projects under subparagraphs 1, 2, 2-2, 2-3, 3, and 4 of Article 8(1), it may, notwithstanding the State Property Act and the Public Property and Commodity Management Act, lease to the Authority, without charge, State or local government property necessary for the relevant project, or permit the Authority to use and profit from such property without charge. <Amended on June 1, 2012>
(2) The Authority shall not construct buildings or other permanent structures on State or local government property leased to it or for which permission for use and profit has been granted under paragraph (1). However, this shall not apply where the property is intended to be contributed to the capital of the Authority after those structures are completed.

Article 28 (Sublease of State or Local Government Property, Etc.)
(1) Where necessary for the efficient management and operation of port facilities, the Authority may sublease State or local government property leased to it or for which it has been granted permission for use and profit under Article 27, or contributed in the form of a right to manage port facilities under Article 6(1). <Amended on June 1, 2012>
(2) Where the Authority intends to sublease property under paragraph (1) (excluding a sublease of State or local government property contributed in the form of a right to manage port facilities under Article 6(1)), it shall prepare a plan in advance and obtain approval from the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries or the head of the local government. The same shall apply where the Authority intends to change approved matters. <Amended on March 23, 2013; December 20, 2016>
(3) Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries intends to approve a sublease or an amendment thereto under paragraph (2), the Minister shall consult in advance with the head of the central administrative agency that leased the relevant State property. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
(4) A person who has obtained a sublease of State or local government property under paragraph (1) shall not construct buildings or other permanent structures on that property. However, this shall not apply to structures that the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries or the head of the local government deems necessary for administrative purposes or for the performance of the Authority's affairs, where construction is conditional upon donation of the structures. <Amended on March 23, 2013>

Article 28-2 (Construction of Permanent Structures on Assets Subject to a Right to Manage Port Facilities, Etc.)
(1) The Authority shall not construct buildings or other permanent structures on assets subject to a right to manage port facilities contributed to it under Article 6(1). However, this shall not apply where construction does not impede the use and enjoyment of the assets, can enhance their utility, and is deemed necessary by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries in consultation with the Minister of Finance and Economy. <Amended on March 23, 2013; October 1, 2025>
(2) Article 18(2) of the State Property Act shall not apply where buildings or other permanent structures are constructed under the proviso to paragraph (1).

Article 29 (Lease of Port Facilities)
(1) The Authority may allow other persons to use port facilities under its management or lease such facilities to other persons.
(2) Where the Authority leases port facilities under paragraph (1), the lease period shall not exceed 50 years.

Article 30 (Collection of Usage Fees and Rent)
(1) The Authority (including a corporation entrusted with projects for the management and operation of passenger terminals and other facilities under Article 42(1); hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article and Article 30-2) may collect usage fees or rent from persons who intend to use or lease port facilities under its management. In such cases, the types of usage fees or rent that the Authority may collect shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on June 1, 2012>
(2) All or part of the usage fees under paragraph (1) may be exempted in cases prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as use for administrative purposes of the State or a local government.
(3) Where the Authority collects usage fees under paragraph (1), it shall determine usage fee rates and other relevant matters for each category, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, and report them to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries. The same shall apply where the Authority intends to change reported matters. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
(4) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall notify the Authority whether a report or an amended report under paragraph (3) is accepted within seven days from the date of receipt of the report. <Newly inserted on January 8, 2019>
(5) Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries fails to notify the Authority, within the period prescribed in paragraph (4), whether the report is accepted or whether the processing period is extended under statutes and regulations governing the processing of civil petitions, the report shall be deemed accepted on the day following the last day of that period (meaning the extended processing period where the processing period is extended or further extended under statutes and regulations governing the processing of civil petitions). <Newly inserted on January 8, 2019>
(6) Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries deems it necessary for smooth port logistics, the Minister may order a change or adjustment to the usage fee rates reported under paragraph (3). <Amended on March 23, 2013; January 8, 2019>

Article 30-2 (Compulsory Collection)
(1) Where a person obliged to pay usage fees or rent for port facilities under Article 30(1) fails to pay them by the due date, the Authority may, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, entrust collection of the usage fees or rent to the Special Self-Governing Province Governor, mayor, county head, or district head (meaning the head of an autonomous district; hereinafter the same shall apply) having jurisdiction over the relevant port. <Amended on December 20, 2016>
(2) Where a Special Self-Governing Province Governor, mayor, county head, or district head is entrusted with collection under paragraph (1), that official shall collect the amount in accordance with the procedures for collection of local taxes in arrears. In such cases, the Authority shall pay to the relevant Special Self-Governing Province, city, county, or district (meaning an autonomous district) an amount prescribed by Presidential Decree out of the amount collected by the Special Self-Governing Province Governor, mayor, county head, or district head. <Amended on December 20, 2016; March 21, 2017>
(3) Where the Authority entrusts collection of usage fees or rent under paragraph (1), it shall submit relevant materials requested by the Special Self-Governing Province Governor, mayor, county head, or district head concerned. <Amended on December 20, 2016>

Article 31 (Handling of Cargo Remaining for Long Periods)
Where the Authority performs duties concerning the handling of cargo remaining at a port for a long period, Article 86 of the Harbor Act shall apply mutatis mutandis. In such cases, "Minister of Oceans and Fisheries" and "State" shall each be construed as "Authority". <Amended on March 23, 2013 and January 29, 2020>

Article 32 (Disposition of Profits and Losses)
(1) Where a profit results from the settlement of accounts for each business year, the Authority shall dispose of it in the following order: <Amended on June 1, 2012>
1. Covering losses carried forward;
2. Setting aside at least two-tenths of the profit as a profit reserve until the reserve reaches one-half of the capital;
3. Distribution to contributors;
4. Setting aside a business expansion reserve.
(2) Where a loss results from the settlement of accounts for each business year, the Authority shall cover it with the business expansion reserve under paragraph (1) 4; where that reserve is insufficient, it shall cover the loss with the profit reserve under paragraph (1) 2. Any loss remaining thereafter shall be carried forward to the next business year. <Amended on June 1, 2012>
(3) The profit reserve and business expansion reserve under paragraph (1) 2 and 4 may be transferred to capital as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on June 1, 2012>

Article 33 (Borrowing of Funds)
The Authority may, following a resolution of the Committee, borrow funds or materials necessary to carry out its business (including borrowings of funds or materials from abroad).

Article 34 (Issuance of Corporate Bonds, Etc.)
(1) The Authority may issue corporate bonds, following a resolution of the Committee, to raise funds necessary to carry out its business.
(2) To issue corporate bonds pursuant to paragraph (1), the Authority shall establish a corporate bond issuance plan that includes the purpose, amount, use, etc. of the corporate bonds to be issued in the relevant year, and obtain approval from the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries following a resolution of the Committee. The same shall apply to any intended amendment of an approved corporate bond issuance plan. <Newly Inserted on December 20, 2016>
(3) The periods of extinctive prescription for corporate bonds shall expire after five years for principal and two years for interest, calculated from the redemption date. <Amended on December 20, 2016>
(4) The amount of corporate bonds issued shall not exceed four times the sum of the Authority's capital and reserves. <Amended on December 20, 2016>
(5) Matters necessary for the issuance of corporate bonds, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (4), shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on December 20, 2016>

Article 35 (Guarantee of Repayment)
The State may guarantee repayment of the principal of and interest on the Authority's corporate bonds and borrowings.

Article 36 (Subsidization of Expenses, Etc.)
The State or a local government may, within budgetary limits, subsidize or lend the funds necessary for projects entrusted pursuant to Article 8 (1) 4 and for non-revenue-generating projects carried out by the Authority that are prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on June 1, 2012>

CHAPTER 5 SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS <Amended on February 4, 2010>

Article 36-2 (Establishment and Operation of the Council for Port Authority Operations)
(1) Where necessary to discuss and coordinate matters requiring consultation among Authorities, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may establish and operate a Council for Port Authority Operations composed of relevant public officials, officers and employees of Authorities, etc.
(2) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Council for Port Authority Operations under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 37 (Guidance and Supervision)
The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may guide and supervise the Authority with respect to matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as port safety, to ensure the soundness of the Authority's finances and the public nature of port management. <Amended on March 23, 2013>

Article 37-2 (Requests for Provision of Materials)
Where necessary for its duties, the Authority may request relevant administrative agencies or other relevant persons to provide materials.

Article 38 (Liability of Officers)
(1) Article 399 (1), Article 400, and Article 401 of the Commercial Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the liability of officers (excluding the auditor).
(2) Articles 414 and 415 of the Commercial Act (in the case of Article 415, limited to the part applying Article 400 mutatis mutandis) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the liability of the Authority's auditor.

Article 39 (Prohibition of Disclosure of Secrets, Etc.)
Members of the Committee and current or former officers and employees of the Authority shall not divulge or misappropriate secrets learned in the course of their duties.

Article 40 (Deeming Persons Public Officials for Purposes of Applying Penalty Provisions)
Officers and employees of the Authority shall be deemed public officials for purposes of applying Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act.

Article 40-2

Article 40-3

Article 41 (Delegation of Authority)
The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may delegate part of the authority under this Act to the heads of subordinate agencies, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on March 23, 2013 and December 20, 2016>

Article 41-2

Article 42 (Entrustment of Business, Etc.)
(1) The Authority may entrust part of its business concerning port guarding and security and the management and operation of passenger terminals, etc. under Article 8 (1) 1 to a corporation established with a capital contribution from the Authority or a corporation prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, the Authority may provide financial assistance for expenses necessary for the entrustment. <Amended on June 1, 2012>
(2) The Authority or a corporation entrusted with business pursuant to paragraph (1) may collect the expenses incurred in performing duties concerning port guarding and security (hereinafter referred to as "security fees") from persons earning revenue through the use of the relevant port. <Amended on June 1, 2012>
(3) When collecting security fees pursuant to paragraph (2), the Authority or a corporation entrusted with business pursuant to paragraph (1) shall determine the types, rates, etc. of security fees as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and report them to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries. The same shall apply to any intended change to the reported matters. <Newly Inserted on June 1, 2012 and March 23, 2013>
(4) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall notify the reporting party whether a report or report of changes under paragraph (3) has been accepted within seven days from the date of its receipt. <Newly Inserted on January 8, 2019>
(5) Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries does not notify the reporting party, within the period prescribed in paragraph (4), whether the report has been accepted or that the processing period has been extended under statutes and regulations concerning the processing of civil petitions, the report shall be deemed accepted on the day following the date that period expires (where the processing period has been extended or further extended under statutes and regulations concerning the processing of civil petitions, the relevant processing period). <Newly Inserted on January 8, 2019>
(6) Where deemed necessary for smooth port logistics, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may order a change or adjustment to the rates of security fees reported pursuant to paragraph (3). <Newly Inserted on June 1, 2012, March 23, 2013 and January 8, 2019>
(7) A person who has paid security fees pursuant to paragraph (2) shall be exempt from the port facility security fees under Article 42 (1) of the Act on the Security of Ships on International Voyages and Port Facilities. <Newly Inserted on June 1, 2012 and January 8, 2019>

CHAPTER 6 PENALTY PROVISIONS <Newly Inserted on February 4, 2010>

Article 43 (Penalty Provisions)
A person who divulges secrets learned in the course of their duties in violation of Article 39 shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than two years or by a fine not exceeding 20 million won. <Amended on October 15, 2014>

Article 44 (Penalty Provisions)
A person who uses land or facilities without filing a report and before receiving a certificate confirming completion of construction, in violation of Article 24 (4), shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than one year or by a fine not exceeding 10 million won. <Amended on October 15, 2014>

Article 45 (Administrative Fines)
(1) A person who uses the name "port authority" in violation of Article 9 shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding five million won. <Amended on March 18, 2014>
(2) The administrative fines under paragraph (1) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
